A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable main text, figures, tables, mathematical examples, references, and Appendices A–B. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: The authors analyze their collected literature through annual publication counts in Figure 5. This qualifies as original descriptive data analysis, although v1 reports no original solver experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains the original literature-count analysis in Figure 5. These retained descriptive results qualify even though no new solver experiments are reported.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes a new solving algorithm or model. The surveyed architectures and procedures remain unchanged; GPG, newly displayed in Figure 4, was already discussed in v1 Section 3.2.3.

E1.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical dataset and task entries, and the literature corpus retains the same coverage. Neither version adds training or evaluation on the cataloged datasets.

E2.justification: Neither version conducts a comparison of a proposed solver against baselines. The surveyed method inventory remains unchanged; adding GPG to Figure 4 does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The literature-selection procedure and Figure 5's April 2025 cutoff remain unchanged. Section 4.1.1 clarifies descriptions of existing metrics without documenting a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 3's illustrative problems and Appendix A's dataset-gap analysis are retained. No ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or substantive case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report publication counts without uncertainty estimates and provide no original repeated-run or seed-based experiments. Section 4.2.2's discussion of averaging evaluations remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 5 retains identical annual counts, including 111 papers in 2024 and 84 through April 2025. Tables 1–4 have identical bodies, and no new performance results or substantively different findings are reported.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theoretical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. The changes to descriptions of maj@k and choice explain existing metrics rather than introduce new mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: surveying tasks, deep learning methods, evaluation, and challenges and future directions. Rephrasing does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 changes CircularEval's stated purpose from reducing 'chance error' to mitigating positional bias and describes mitigation efforts more cautiously as attempts. The broader interpretations and limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1.1 now specifies four candidate answers for choice and random selection when the model output matches none, refining the previously generic scoring description. This is additional documentation; the survey-search details and resource links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and positioning relative to earlier surveys remain unchanged. GPG's addition to Figure 4 redisplays an already cited method, and the bibliography is retained.

P1.justification: v5 polishes the abstract, selected introduction and discussion passages, and Appendices A–B while retaining their organization. It also standardizes terminology, renames B.3 to Geometric Figure Retrieval, and inadvertently duplicates B.4's opening sentence.

P2.justification: Figure 4 adds GPG to its existing reinforcement-learning examples and shortens some citation labels. Table captions receive capitalization and wording edits, with minor layout reflow; the figures and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the choice scoring procedure and CircularEval's purpose more explicit, improves awkward prose, and aligns Figure 4 with the existing GPG discussion. These provide a limited gain in clarity and usefulness. The duplicated sentence in Appendix B.4 is a small editorial regression, while the underlying coverage and evidence remain unchanged.
